A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DSoftKI research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic-function and MD22 experiments, including prediction errors, negative log-likelihoods, interpolation ablations, and training curves.

after.justification: v2 reports original results on the retained benchmarks and adds timing measurements, an objective ablation, n-body and UCI experiments, and a deep-kernel evaluation.

M1.justification: Appendix D adds DSoftKI-DKL, using a jointly trained two-layer neural feature extractor and an RBF kernel in a learned 24-dimensional space. This implements an extension only proposed as future work in v1; the principal local-temperature interpolation and posterior-inference procedure remain.

E1.justification: The five synthetic functions and seven MD22 molecules are retained. New Appendix C adds four gravitational n-body settings with 24–60 input dimensions and six regression datasets with synthetic gradients: Kin40k, Protein, Bike, Elevators, Pol, and Slice. These substantially broaden the represented domains and gradient-observation conditions.

E2.justification: The original synthetic and MD22 comparator sets are retained. Appendix D adds direct comparisons between DSoftKI and its new DSoftKI-DKL variant in Tables 14–16. The additional n-body and UCI comparisons reuse DDSVGP.

E3.justification: v2 adds per-epoch wall-clock timing and new experimental protocols: a 90/10 n-body split after filtering high-gradient samples, three-neighbor gradient estimation for UCI, and separate GP/neural learning rates for DKL. The original synthetic 10000/10000 split and effective-learning-rate controls remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix B.2 compares exact-MLL-only and Hutchinson-only training, testing the stability and accuracy rationale for the existing switching objective. Appendix D examines learned-feature accuracy versus computational cost, and Appendix C.2 tests estimated, noisy gradients. Existing interpolation, noise-ratio, and training-curve analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report three-run averages for the principal experiments and standard-deviation training curves. v2 additionally explains unavailable uncertainty caused by unstable runs, distinguishing ±nan from complete failure in Table 7 and identifying failed SoftKI runs in Tables 2, 3, and 8. No increase in repetitions is stated.

E6.justification: Numerous retained scores and plots change; for example, DSoftKI's Welch value NLL changes from -3.742 ± 0.945 to -1.14 ± 4.795 in Table 3 under the same stated synthetic setup. Substantial new results cover runtime, objective stability, n-body/UCI prediction, and DKL's faster training with higher prediction errors.

T1.justification: v2 revises the interpolation derivative and componentwise temperature algebra, including adding the missing leading minus sign in v1 Equation 18. It also changes the pseudoloss expression and adds a trace-estimator derivation in Equations 12–15. These are localized mathematical revisions without a new central theorem.

C1.justification: The central claims of scalable, accurate full-derivative GP regression remain. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion now present learned-kernel compatibility as demonstrated, including dimensionality-reduction speedups, whereas v1's conclusion left deep-kernel learning for future investigation.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of runtime costs, complementary local-temperature/global-lengthscale roles, and DKL's accuracy–speed tradeoff. It also removes v1 Appendix B.1's general assertion that increasing value weighting tends to improve performance, retaining the dataset-dependent qualification.

D1.justification: New disclosures include initialization values and k-means initialization in Appendix B.1, GPU hardware for timing, n-body simulation and filtering instructions, UCI gradient construction, and DKL architecture and learning rates. The code pointer changes from softki_gp_kit to dsoftki_gp. These substantially improve implementation and experimental documentation.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for UCI, Girard and Hutchinson trace estimation, Plummer softening, and SciPy. The main positioning against derivative variational GPs and kernel interpolation remains. The SoftKI reference's preprint-to-publication update represents the same cited work.

P1.justification: The main section structure and much existing prose remain. Local rewrites clarify temperature terminology and mathematical notation, update the abstract and conclusion, and introduce appendix navigation. Former Appendix C becomes Appendix E after the new dataset and DKL appendices.

P2.justification: v2 adds substantial table displays for timing, objective ablation, n-body/UCI results, and DKL accuracy and speed. Existing figures and tables are retained with updated captions and placement; Figures 7–8 are grouped together, and the temperature and lengthscale histograms exchange Figure 9–10 numbering.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens assessment of the paper's central scalability and stability claims: v1 lacked wall-clock comparisons and an objective ablation, while v2 supplies both in Tables 4, 6, and 7, alongside important initialization details. Broader evaluations and the implemented DKL extension add useful validation. The evidence also exposes costs: DSoftKI can train slower than DDSVGP, and DKL gains speed while increasing error. These documented tradeoffs improve the paper's informativeness.
